level.description: The value of a rule: a level (error, warn, info or off), true for the default level of the rule, or false for off.

severity.description: The level of a rule: error (fails the run), warn, info or off.

description: The configuration file of jactionlint, .github/jactionlint.yaml. Generated from the rule registry by `jactionlint --print-config-schema`. See https://jactionlint.jdx.dev/config

assume-default-permissions.description: What to assume for a caller workflow which declares no permissions: restricted is GitHub's restricted default token, permissive is write on every scope except id-token. Unset assumes nothing.

baseline.description: The baseline of accepted findings. auto (or true) applies .github/jactionlint-baseline.json when the file exists, false or no value applies none, and any other value is the path of the baseline file relative to the repository root, which must exist. The --baseline flag overrides it.

check-falsy-ternary.description: Deprecated: turn on the unsound-ternary rule.

check-workflow-run-names.description: Deprecated: turn on the workflow-run-names rule.

config-secrets.description: Names of the secrets of your repository or organization. When it is a list, the secrets context is checked against it (an empty list allows none; GITHUB_TOKEN is always allowed). null disables the check.

config-variables.description: Names of the configuration variables of your repository or organization. When it is a list, the vars context is checked against it (an empty list allows none). null disables the check.

extends.description: Config files to inherit from. Relative paths are resolved from the directory of this file. Later files win over earlier ones and this file wins over all of them.

rules.description: Apply only the fixes of these rules, like --fix-rules (which overrides it). All fixes are applied when the list is empty.

generated-files.description: What to do with a file whose first comment says that a tool wrote it (DO NOT EDIT, automatically generated by ...): skip-policy (the default) does not report the rules of the policy and style groups there, report treats it like any other file, skip reports nothing.

ignores.description: Findings to accept, matched by the rule and by where they are (file, job, step, uses) instead of by line, so they survive tools which rewrite the workflow. At least one of file, uses, job and step is required.

expires.description: The last day (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC) the entry accepts findings. After it the findings come back and the expired-ignore rule reports the entry. Quote it ("2027-06-30") if your editor reads an unquoted date as a timestamp, which has no string type.

file.description: A glob matched against the path of the file, relative to the repository root (** crosses directories).

reason.description: Why the finding is accepted. It is for the readers of the file.

rule.description: The rule ID, or a list of rule IDs, whose findings are accepted.

step.description: The id or the name of the step.

uses.description: The uses value of the step or of the called workflow: a pattern like actions/checkout or actions/*, a glob for other values (docker://alpine*), or a regular expression between slashes (/^actions\/(checkout|cache)@/).

max-run-lines.description: Deprecated: the max option of the max-run-lines rule.

online.description: Turns on the checks which query the GitHub API for the files this configuration applies to, like the --online flag. The default is false: nothing uses the network.

online-options.description: Tunes the online checks. Every key is optional. The command line flags win over them.

allow.description: Look up only the repositories matching one of these owner/repo patterns (* is a wildcard within a part). Empty allows all.

api-url.description: The REST API URL of a GitHub Enterprise Server, like https://ghe.example.com/api/v3. A token is not sent to a host named here by the config file of a repository.

cache-ttl.description: How long a cached answer is used without asking GitHub again, as a duration like 1h. 0s always revalidates. The default is 1h.

concurrency.description: How many requests are in flight at most (at most 32; 0 is the default, 6).

deny.description: Never look up the repositories matching one of these owner/repo patterns. It wins over allow.

gh-cli.description: Whether gh auth token is asked for a token when no variable or file has one. The default is true.

max-rate-limit-wait.description: The longest to wait for a rate limit to reset, as a duration like 30s. 0s never waits. The default is 30s.

mode.description: cache never uses the network and answers from the disk cache, strict makes the exit status 3 when a lookup is skipped, cache,strict is both. A mode other than the default also turns the online checks on, unless online is false.

retries.description: How often a request is repeated after a server error or a secondary rate limit (at most 10). The default is 2.

token-env.description: The name of the environment variable which holds the token. It is read before GITHUB_TOKEN and GH_TOKEN.

token-file.description: A file which holds the token.

additionalProperties.description: The configuration of the files matching the pattern.

ignore.description: Rule IDs and regular expressions. A rule ID ignores all the findings of the rule, and a regular expression ignores the findings whose message matches it.

paths.description: Configuration for the files matching a glob pattern, relative to the repository root. The path separator is always /.

platform.description: The system which runs the workflows: github (the default), or forgejo or gitea, which also accept `uses: https://host/owner/repo@ref` for an action. That form stays an error on github.

profile.description: The set of rules which run: correctness (what actionlint checks and the bug detectors of jactionlint), default (adds the security posture and policy rules worth failing a build on) or pedantic (adds the noisy and opinionated rules). Each profile includes the one before it. The --profile flag overrides it. The retired names strict and all mean pedantic.

require-checkout-before-local-action.description: Deprecated: turn on the local-action-checkout rule.

require-commit-hash.description: Deprecated: turn on the unpinned-uses rule.

require-expression-wrapping.description: Deprecated: turn on the require-expression-wrapping rule.

require-permissions.description: Deprecated: turn on the missing-permissions rule.

require-shell.description: Deprecated: turn on the require-shell rule.

required-actions.description: Actions or reusable workflows which must be used at least once in every checked workflow. The check is off when the list is empty.

action.description: The name of the action, like actions/checkout, without @version. A sub-path is part of the name. It is case-insensitive.

version.description: The exact ref (tag, branch or commit SHA) which one use of the action must have. Any version is accepted when it is omitted.

rules.description: The level and the options of each rule by its rule ID. A rule which is not listed follows the profile. See https://jactionlint.jdx.dev/rules

action-syntax.description: The action metadata does not follow the syntax of action.yml. Group: correctness. Profile: correctness. Default level: error. https://jactionlint.jdx.dev/rules#action-syntax

policies.description: How strongly to pin the images matching a pattern: hash-pin (a digest, the default of require-digest), tag-pin (a tag other than latest, or a digest) or any. The most specific pattern that matches wins over require-digest: more literal characters before the first *, in the pattern with the registry written out, then fewer *, then a tag, then the longer pattern. Patterns are globs of the image name, where * matches any characters: "*", "ghcr.io/my-org/*", "registry.example.com/team/tool" or "node:20". The registry of Docker Hub can be left out ("node" is "docker.io/library/node").
